A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphOmni and retain matching benchmark components, experiments, and RL optimization. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM evaluations, error analyses, and RL search experiments, including Tables 3–4 and the additional Qwen3 results in Appendix D.6.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and RL results and reports additional experiments on real-world graphs, larger graphs, NP-hard tasks, and prompt perturbations.

M1.justification: The core graph generators, serialization formats, prompt schemes, and DQN selector retain their procedures. The objective, network architecture, and Algorithm 1 match v2 Appendix C and v4 Appendix D. Correcting LTM from long-term memory to least-to-most prompting does not change the retained prompt examples.

E1.justification: v4 adds social/interaction graphs from IMDB-MULTI, molecular graphs from ogbg-molhiv, and Hamiltonian cycle and Max-Cut tasks. It also evaluates 30–50 and 50–100 node graphs and linguistically perturbed BFS prompts. These extend the domains, task requirements, and test conditions beyond v2's canonical synthetic-graph evaluation.

E2.justification: Qwen-2.5 (72B) is newly evaluated. Qwen-3 also joins the detailed prompt-by-format heatmap comparisons, although its model-level evaluation already appeared in v2 Table 16. Llama-3 and GPT-4o-mini remain in v4 Table 13 despite their omission from the representative main-text table.

E3.justification: New protocols include balanced Hamiltonian-cycle labels with explicit tour validation, Max-Cut size-and-partition checking, and a 4,000-instance BFS perturbation evaluation using two models. Output-token and monetary-cost measurements add evaluation metrics. Section 2 also revises the stated Easy range from 0–10 to 5–10 nodes; this correction does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds generator structural comparisons, a scaling-versus-reasoning analysis, graph-type sensitivity profiles, output-length and cost analyses, computational-complexity comparisons, and prompt-paraphrase robustness tests. Larger and real-world graph experiments additionally examine generalization. The earlier error cases and input/output examples are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means with 95% confidence intervals and standard errors for input-token plots. v4 extends these practices to additional results without introducing repeated-run counts, seed reporting, significance tests, or a revised uncertainty-estimation procedure. Its new sensitivity metrics measure variation across experimental factors.

E6.justification: v4 substantially expands reported outcomes and revises existing Qwen-3 and cycle-detection results. For example, o4-mini's Hard cycle accuracy changes from 93.06% in v2 Table 3 to 95.61% in v4 Table 13. The shortest-path random baseline changes from 0% to 50% without an accompanying explanation. These are changes in reported results, not established controlled performance gains; RL-Opt Table 4 remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces mathematical definitions of prompt and format sensitivity through averaged accuracy standard deviations and median-based classifications. Appendix H.1 adds algorithmic-complexity reasoning. The RL objective and Bellman recursion are retained, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v4's abstract and contributions explicitly claim robustness and transferability across larger graphs, real-world domains, and NP-hard tasks, extending the scope of v2's central empirical claims. Efficiency–accuracy analysis becomes an explicit contribution. The multidimensional benchmark and RL selection claims remain; the abstract's 75% cost reduction restates an efficiency claim already supported in v2.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations separating model scaling from reasoning improvements, task understanding from graph parsing, and computational complexity from output-structure difficulty. It argues that real graphs can under-stress reasoning and that synthetic evaluation offers better control. The explicit real-world-data limitation is removed, while new discussions assert generalization and perturbation robustness, sometimes more strongly than the accompanying tables support.

D1.justification: v4 documents paraphrase pools, component extraction, string replacement, and graph-preservation validation in Appendix H.3. It also specifies tokenizers, the source of o4-mini reasoning-token counts, and cost-calculation assumptions, and adds model access information. Code access instructions change to a community repository and include a project page. The expanded main-text DQN description largely reproduces existing appendix details.

R1.justification: Table 1 adds GraphArena and GraphWild, while related work adds GraphAbstract, GraphVista, and newer graph applications and surveys. References also expand to support graph generators, real datasets, and synthetic-evaluation arguments; MMLU-pro is removed. The central positioning around joint evaluation of graph types, serializations, and prompts remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction are rewritten, separate dimension explanations are consolidated, and findings are reordered. RL formalization moves into an expanded main-text discussion, while the appendices are reorganized around new extended-study and ablation sections. Terminology and prompt explanations are also corrected.

P2.justification: The original overview is replaced by an expanded, redrawn evaluation-pipeline figure. Radar charts and heatmaps incorporate additional models, and the main results table becomes a representative subset with complete results in the appendix. New sensitivity plots, efficiency charts, perturbation illustrations, and experimental tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence addressing v2's limited graph scale and synthetic-only coverage, together with stronger implementation documentation. However, new interpretations conflict with their evidence: Appendix C.2 claims uniformly higher real-graph cycle accuracy although Table 9 mostly shows decreases, and H.2 claims uniform scaling degradation although Table 31 reports o4-mini diameter accuracy increasing from 34.61% to 40.44%. The unexplained shortest-path baseline change further complicates interpretation. These substantial evidential gains and added consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
